checks: For a fixed direction, each finite assigned group covers its entire current fibers with actual buffered cap bound q_i(t), while the old strict gaps off the deepest bases persist. Dividing by M−tD+o(t) gives first improvement (ℓ_i−βD)/M. Including the penalty adds +τs in improvement units. Since ℓ_i≥ℓ_i^0, strict positivity of all conservative mass-unit improvements contradicts an attained local minimum over actual compatible families.

Every finite list of continuous normal-dependent convex fields realizes every nonnegative coefficient combination by the same body deformation. Cap normals are independent signed coordinates by cap copy and shared across the contacts of their group; the interior-scale coordinate has both signs. The finite admissible coefficient cone is closed and convex. A strict separator from its negative polar would lie in the coefficient cone and yield a positive lower bound across all branches, contrary to the no-descent conclusion.

The group/contact/selector coefficient space is a finite disjoint union of compact weak-star products. The coareas have positive lower and finite upper bounds for the fixed menu, so the branch evaluations are continuous. For each finite coefficient restriction a finite probability mixture exists by the compact convex-hull intersection. The closed averaged test conditions on compact regular Borel probabilities have the finite-intersection property, giving one probability for the whole class without any finite-support assertion for that probability.

The fractions ρ_ij/(B_i^θ T_ij) sum to one within each branch. Averaging an outside selector with those exact cap weights preserves its boundary loss, coarea, and full first moment by linearity in the selector. Multiplying its effective coarea by ω_ij gives ρ_ij κ_i. Positive group mass makes every cap weight positive, and the signed cap equations give the κ-weighted contact barycenter minus the corresponding weighted covariance shift.

Averaging the contact coefficient gives positive own-energy and own-volume kernels, and the pooled covariance contribution with factor 1/(2M). Normalizing the objective contributes −βD. The contact total-mass coefficient is −(d+2)Δ/(2dM), since 1/(d+1)+1/[d(d+1)]+1/2=(d+2)/(2d). The optional signed scale coefficient is Mτ−Δ. On inside support the body selector stays one and the section selector stays zero; outside, the same effective selector enters both. Hence 0≤W≤1 and the displayed density A is nonnegative.

Testing both signs of continuous normal-weighted affine fields gives equality of normal marginals and their conditional full physical first moments. Testing a nonnegative continuous normal weight times a finite convex physical function gives the localized convex-order inequality. Both measures live on the Borel regular-normal graph in the compact exposed-face relation. The normal-preserving coupling therefore has the full ambient input row mean, and actuality gives active anchored base rows. This is an old-boundary to old-boundary law for A and B_*σ; the discrete deepest contacts and original mixed volume are not its transport marginals.

On the attainment class the sampled f floor and f≤1 give two-sided bounds for δ_ia/ε. Proper own-ball coarea, covariance eigenvalue bounds under Γ-unit normalization, and common outer-radius surface/section bounds give fixed positive bounds on 1/B_i^θ. The probability normalization then yields Δ comparable to ε. The source volume and energy floors, accepted energy-denominator bound and bounded covariance integrands give uniform O(ε) for the three extra density terms. Only sampled source marks enter the upper bound f≤1.

On a zero-weight group all the body/section contributions vanish; its effective outside selectors can be assigned arbitrary values in [0,1]. Uniform bounds concern the compact attainment class, while the local separator uses all allowed physical paths.

The comparison of surface capacities, projective cap credits, and outside-source-face costs remains open in this package.
